Shares rose more than 1% in premarket trading.

“Apple is repositioning iPhone as an intelligent personal hub, with the Duo and Siri AI at the center of this strategy,” Morgan Stanley analyst Erik Woodring wrote in a note to clients. “When coupled with cont’d product innovation (battery, camera, health + more this Spring), clear Semis/SW differentiation and pricing tailwinds, we see above-trend growth into FY27.”

Woodring, who has an Overweight rating and $360 price target on Apple, added that the event “felt different” than past events not only because of new CEO John Ternus but also because the offerings are becoming “more exciting.”

“In our view, [the] event previewed far more innovation than past years – Apple’s first-ever 2nm A20 SoC provides a significant performance leap, the iPhone Duo is likely to redefine premium smartphones, Apple’s SW/HW integration and attention to detail are subtle but game changing, and even Siri AI now shows it will play an important role in turning the iPhone into a consumer’s centralized intelligence hub,” Woodring added.

for the iPhone 18 Pro of $100 compared to previous models was “better than feared.”

“[Given the] iPhone 18 Pro cycle uncertainty over limited hardware upgrades and potential margin pressure, partially offset by the support of iPhone Duo, we see iPhone 18 series as [a] modest product cycle,” Huang wrote in a note to clients. He has a Hold rating on Apple.

J.P. Morgan analyst Samik Chatterjee said the event was “largely in line” with his expectations, though investors may have expected larger price hikes due to rising memory costs. (Apple also raised the price of its existing older iPhone models by $100.)
“Most importantly, we see the pricing decisions as supportive of a positive volume cycle,” Chatterjee wrote in a note to clients.

“The combination of Siri AI- led features leveraging Apple’s foundational models, set to be released in Beta in mid-September, and volume support from favorable pricing decisions, should together help in robust iPhone revenue growth; expect supply chain feedback on volumes following the early weeks of ordering to be a positive catalyst for the shares,” Chatterjee added.
